mainTopic: How the כהנים get atonement on יום הכפורים and the two confessions of the פר, then the new משנה on the four kinds of forgotten awareness of טומאה and the holiness of the added עזרה.
overview: The ברייתא finishes explaining how the כהנים are forgiven for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו on יום הכפורים. It rules that the פר of אהרן covers them, not the inner שעיר, and backs this up with the פסוק 'בית אהרן'. The גמרא then defends the ברייתא's sources. 'אשר לעם' is free, because public funding is learned from another פסוק. The double 'אשר לו' is really about the כהן גדול paying from his own money, and the ברייתא was solving a logic problem about who pays. Next the גמרא returns to the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about the שעיר המשתלח. It asks why, according to רבי יהודה, the bull needs two confessions. The answer is that the כהן גדול first atones for himself and then for his household, since an innocent person should atone for the guilty. After the הדרן closing פרק שבועות שתים, a new משנה lists the four kinds of forgotten awareness for eating קודש or entering the מקדש while טמא, which require a קרבן עולה ויורד. It adds that an addition to the עזרה is fully holy, because it is made through a king, a נביא, the אורים ותומים, a סנהדרין of 71, and a formal procession.

steps.title: The כהנים get atonement through the פר of אהרן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that the כהנים are forgiven for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו through the פר of אהרן, not through the inner שעיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהנים also need atonement for defiling the מקדש and its sacred foods. Through what are they forgiven? It is better that the פר of אהרן covers them, because that offering was already widened to include his household. The inner שעיר should not cover them, because nothing ever widened it beyond 'the people'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing its point: the כהנים are left out of the inner שעיר, so it decides which offering forgives them instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both offerings have a basic group they cover: the פר covers אהרן, and the שעיר covers the people. The פר already reaches past its basic group to include 'his household', so stretching it to all כהנים is a small step. The שעיר was never stretched at all, so it makes more sense to place the כהנים under the פר.

keyTerms.meaning: Entering the מקדש or eating sacred food while impure
The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום הכפורים
Its basic rule was loosened or widened
The goat whose blood is sprinkled inside the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: for defiling the Temple and its sacred foods.
Through what do they get atonement?
It is better that they get atonement through Aaron's bull,
since its rule was already widened for his household;
phrases.notes: The bull is mainly for אהרן himself, but the תורה already widens it to cover his household too.

phrases.english: and they should not get atonement through the goat done inside,
since its rule was never widened.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמָּה הֵם מִתְכַּפְּרִין? מוּטָב שֶׁיִּתְכַּפְּרוּ בְּפָרוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section, which excluded the כהנים from the inner שעיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים are forgiven for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו through the פר of אהרן.
steps.whatToRemember: The פר of אהרן covers all the כהנים, because it already reaches past אהרן to 'his household'.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the כהנים have no atonement at all. They are only left out of the שעיר; the פר covers them instead.

steps.title: A פסוק shows all כהנים are אהרן's house
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא backs up its logic with a פסוק that calls all the כהנים 'house of אהרן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to push back on that reasoning, look at the פסוק: 'House of אהרן, bless ה'.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a פסוק to support its ruling, in case someone doubts the logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic in step 1 could be challenged, so the ברייתא brings a firmer source. The פסוק uses 'house of אהרן' for the whole family of כהנים. That means 'his household' in the פר's פסוק can include all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish to say (an introduction to a backup proof)
House of אהרן, meaning the family of כהנים

phrases.english: And if you wish to say otherwise,
behold, it says:
"House of Aaron, bless the Lord, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם נַפְשְׁךָ לוֹמַר – הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a פסוק to support the reasoning of step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the פר of אהרן atones for all the כהנים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים: בית אהרן ברכו את ה'

steps.title: What does 'if you wish to say' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what objection the ברייתא had in mind when it said 'ואם נפשך לומר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the ברייתא mean by 'and if you wish to say'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask what pushback the ברייתא was answering. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ואם נפשך לומר' suggests that someone could reject the first argument. The גמרא wants to name that rejection so we understand why the פסוק was needed.

phrases.english: And what is meant by "if you wish to say"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the phrase that opened step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What objection the ברייתא was answering with its פסוק.

steps.title: All priests are called 'his household'
steps.stepSummary: The objection is that 'ביתו' means only אהרן's close family; the answer is that all כהנים are called his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you would say the פסוק of the פר says 'his household', so it covers only his own family, the answer is that all the כהנים are called 'his household', as it says: 'House of אהרן, bless ה'; those who fear ה', bless ה'.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the objection the ברייתא had in mind and shows how the פסוק answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might read 'ביתו' narrowly, as אהרן's immediate family only, and then the other כהנים would not be covered. The פסוק in תהלים uses 'house of אהרן' for all כהנים. So 'ביתו' can include every כהן.

phrases.english: And if you would say "his household" is written, so only his own family is covered,
the answer is that all of them are called "his household,"
as it says: "House of Aaron, bless the Lord,
those who fear the Lord, bless the Lord."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The objection is that 'ביתו' means only close family; the פסוק shows all כהנים are called 'house of אהרן'.

steps.title: Isn't 'for the people' needed for something else?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's use of 'אשר לעם', since those words seem needed to teach that the goat must be bought with public money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the phrase 'which is for the people' really come to teach this? It is needed to teach that the Torah requires the goat to come from the people!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the source the ברייתא used to exclude the כהנים from the שעיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A phrase in the תורה usually teaches one thing. If 'אשר לעם' teaches that the goat is paid for by the community, it is already used up. Then it cannot also teach that the כהנים are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: And this phrase "which is for the people,"
does it come for this?!
This phrase is needed for
what the Merciful One says: it must come from the people!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the ברייתא's source for excluding the כהנים from the שעיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'אשר לעם' to exclude the כהנים from the inner שעיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase is already needed to teach that the goat must be bought with public funds, so it cannot also teach the exclusion.

steps.title: Public funding comes from a different verse
steps.stepSummary: The rule that the goat comes from public money is learned from 'ומאת עדת בני ישראל', so 'אשר לעם' is free.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule comes from the פסוק 'And from the congregation of the children of Israel he shall take two goats.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the public-funding rule has its own source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the funding rule is learned from 'ומאת עדת בני ישראל', the words 'אשר לעם' are not needed for it. They can therefore teach that the inner שעיר does not cover the כהנים, as the ברייתא said.

keyTerms.meaning: The congregation of the children of Israel

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא מִ״וּמֵאֵת עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ נָפְקָא.
phrases.english: That rule is derived from "And from the congregation of the children of Israel."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִ״וּמֵאֵת עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ נָפְקָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to another source for the competing teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אשר לעם' is needed to teach that the goat is publicly funded.
steps.terutzMaskana: Public funding is learned from 'ומאת עדת בני ישראל', so 'אשר לעם' is free to exclude the כהנים.
steps.whatToRemember: Each teaching needs its own source: 'ומאת עדת בני ישראל' teaches public funding, and 'אשר לעם' teaches that the כהנים are left out of the שעיר.

steps.title: The words 'his own' are needed for a different law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא again: 'אשר לו' seems needed to teach that the כהן גדול buys the פר with his own money, not public money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does 'his own' really come to teach that? It is needed for another ברייתא: he brings the bull from his own money, not from public money.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as it did with 'אשר לעם', the גמרא now questions the ברייתא's use of 'אשר לו'. It says those words already have a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא used 'אשר לו' to say the פר atones only for אהרן and his house. But another ברייתא uses the same words to teach a money rule: the כהן גדול must pay for the פר himself. If the words are used up for that rule, they can't also teach who gets כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That is his own', a phrase about the כהן גדול's bull
It is needed for (a different teaching)

phrases.english: And this phrase 'his own' —
does it come to teach this?!
It is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא:
He brings it from his own money,
and he does not bring it from the public's money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After 'אשר לעם' was freed up, the גמרא makes the same kind of challenge against 'אשר לו'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'אשר לו' to limit the bull's כפרה to אהרן and his house
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase is already used for the rule that the כהן גדול pays from his own money, so it is not free to teach anything else.

steps.title: The full ברייתא: 'his own' is written twice to make it required
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא. The first 'אשר לו' rules out using the כהנים' money. The second makes the rule required, so a bull bought with other money is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he can't use public money, since the public isn't atoned by it, but he could use his fellow כהנים' money, since they are atoned by it. So the פסוק says 'his own'. One might think that if he did use others' money it still works. So the פסוק repeats 'his own', to make it required.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the rest of the ברייתא from the last step. It shows that both times 'אשר לו' appears, the words are used for the money rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the two appearances of 'אשר לו' for two separate points. The first excludes the כהנים' money too, not just the public's. The second tells us that breaking this rule makes the bull invalid. This makes the challenge stronger, because neither 'אשר לו' seems left over.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק repeated it to make it required, so without it the offering is invalid

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common pattern: when the תורה repeats a requirement, it shows the requirement is מעכב, meaning the offering is invalid without it.

phrases.english: One might think he may not bring it from public money,
because the public is not atoned by it;
but he may bring it from his brothers the כהנים's money,
since his brothers the כהנים are atoned by it?
The פסוק says: 'his own'.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יָבִיא, וְאִם הֵבִיא כָּשֵׁר?
phrases.english: One might think he shouldn't, but if he did, it is valid?
The פסוק says 'his own' again —
phrases.notes: The second 'his own' is in ויקרא 16:11.

phrases.english: the פסוק repeated it to make it required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא that the challenge in step 7 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That both appearances of 'אשר לו' are used for the money rule

steps.title: The ברייתא was answering a logic problem, not reading extra words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא was not limiting the bull's כפרה because of the words 'אשר לו'. It was answering a question: since the כהנים don't pay for the bull, why should it atone for them? The answer is that all כהנים are called 'his house'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what bothered the תנא: why doesn't the people's goat atone for the כהנים? Because they lose no money on it, as it says 'of the people'. But they also lose no money on אהרן's bull! So he said: all the כהנים are called 'his house'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the ברייתא really meant. Its point was to explain why the כהנים are included in the bull's כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule seems to be that you get כפרה from an offering your money paid for. That is why the כהנים, who don't pay for the people's goat, aren't atoned by it. By that rule they shouldn't be atoned by אהרן's bull either, since he pays alone. The ברייתא answers that the כהנים count as אהרן's house, so 'אשר לו' never had to be free.

keyTerms.meaning: It was bothering him, this was his difficulty

steps.whatToRemember: The כהנים get כפרה from the כהן גדול's bull even though they don't pay for it, because all כהנים are called 'his house'. The words 'אשר לו' stay used for the rule that he must pay himself.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say 'אשר לו' has a second job. It says the ברייתא never needed it for limiting the כפרה. Its point came from logic about who pays.

phrases.english: This is what was difficult for the תנא:
Why is the people's goat different, that the כהנים are not atoned by it?
Because they lose no money on it,
as it is written: 'that is for the people';

phrases.aramaic: בִּדְאַהֲרֹן נָמֵי לָא קָא חָסְרִי בֵּיהּ מָמוֹנָא!
phrases.english: with אהרן's bull too, they lose no money on it!
So he said: they are all called 'his house'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 7–8 by explaining what the ברייתא was really doing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the purpose of the ברייתא: it reasons from logic, not from extra words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא learned from 'אשר לו' that the bull atones only for אהרן's house, which would clash with the money rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא was answering why the כהנים, who don't pay, are still atoned. The answer is that they count as 'his house', so 'אשר לו' stays used for the money rule.

steps.title: For רבי שמעון, the bull's three כפרות match the three goats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. It says רבי שמעון's view nicely explains why the bull has two confessions and its blood: one for each of the three goats. This sets up a difficulty for רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי שמעון: that is why the תורה writes two confessions and the bull's blood. One matches the goat done inside, one matches the goat done outside, and one matches the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It shows how well רבי שמעון's view fits the פסוקים, so that it can then ask how רבי יהודה explains them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute is about the שעיר המשתלח: רבי שמעון holds that the כהנים are not atoned by it, so none of the three goats covers them. They need their own כפרה from the bull to match each goat. The bull's two confessions and its blood service give three acts of כפרה, one for each of the three goats.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one view); usually leads to a question on the other view
The goat whose blood is brought inside the קודש הקדשים
The מוסף goat, offered outside on the outer מזבח
The goat sent away to עזאזל

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשלמא' does not end the discussion. It praises one view only to set up a question on the other view.

phrases.english: It works well according to רבי שמעון:

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב תְּרֵי וִידּוּיִן וְדַם הַפָּר,
phrases.english: that is why two confessions and the bull's blood are written,
one matching the goat done inside,
and one matching the goat done outside,
and one matching the goat that is sent away;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the ברייתא and goes back to the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view (the actual question comes next)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוקים fit רבי שמעון's three-to-three match so well, the גמרא will ask what רבי יהודה does with them.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה need two confessions and the bull's blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: if the bull does less atoning in his view, why does it need two confessions and its blood? One confession with its blood should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יהודה, why do I need two confessions and the bull's blood? One confession and its blood would be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the question onto רבי יהודה. In his view the bull seems to have less to do, so why does it need so much?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, רבי שמעון's view explained the bull's two confessions and its blood well, because each one matched one of the three goats. רבי יהודה holds that the כהנים do get atonement through the שעיר המשתלח, together with the people. So the bull only needs to match the two other goats, and one confession plus the blood would be enough. The second confession looks unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: Confession, spoken over the bull by the כהן גדול
The blood of the bull, brought inside and sprinkled

phrases.english: But according to רבי יהודה,

phrases.aramaic: תְּרֵי וִידּוּיִן וְדַם הַפָּר לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: why do I need two confessions and the bull's blood?
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול confesses over his bull twice on יום כיפור, once in ויקרא 16:6 and again in 16:11.

phrases.english: One confession and its blood would be enough!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, תְּרֵי וִידּוּיִן וְדַם הַפָּר לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 10 showed that רבי שמעון explains the bull's parts well. This step is the difficulty that comparison set up for רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view of what the כהן גדול's bull atones for
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the כהנים get atonement through the שעיר המשתלח, the bull only needs to match the inner and outer goats. One confession and the blood cover those two, so a second confession seems unnecessary.

steps.title: One confession for himself, one for his household
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one confession is for the כהן גדול himself and one for his household. It supports this with the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל: it is better for an innocent person to atone for the guilty.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is for himself and one is for his household. As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: This is how justice works: it is better that an innocent person come and atone for the guilty, and not that a guilty person come and atone for the guilty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question on רבי יהודה. The two confessions are needed because the כהן גדול must first get himself clean before he atones for others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even for רבי יהודה, the confessions are not wasted. The first confession makes the כהן גדול himself innocent. Only then does he confess for his household, so he is atoning for others as an innocent person and not as a guilty one.

keyTerms.meaning: One for himself, and one for his household (the כהנים)
A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל
The attribute of justice, meaning how justice works

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול confesses for himself first, so that he can atone for others as an innocent person.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains the order of the יום כיפור service: the כהן גדול always takes care of his own atonement before atoning for others.

phrases.english: One is for himself, and one is for his household.
phrases.notes: 'His household' means all the כהנים, as the גמרא explained in step 9.

phrases.english: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
This is how the attribute of justice works:
It is better that an innocent person come
and atone for the guilty,
and not that a guilty person come
and atone for the guilty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד לוֹ, וְאֶחָד לְבֵיתוֹ. כִּדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 on רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new purpose for the extra confession
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought that for רבי יהודה the second confession had no job, since the כהנים are atoned for through the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two confessions follow an order. First the כהן גדול becomes innocent through his own confession, and then he confesses for his household.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק שבועות שתים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the end of the פרק called שבועות שתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, שבועות שתים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said at the end of a פרק. It marks that פרק שבועות שתים is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not part of the argument. It closes the chapter, and the next line starts a brand new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, said when finishing a פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, שבועות שתים

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final answer in step 12.

steps.title: New משנה: awareness of טומאה is two that are four
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with a משנה saying that awareness of טומאה comes in two kinds that are really four. It starts with the first case: a person knew he was טמא, then forgot his טומאה, but remembered the food was holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Awareness of טומאה is two that are four. He became טמא and knew it. Then his טומאה was hidden from him, but he remembered that it was holy.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the kinds of awareness that matter for someone who ate holy food or entered the מקדש while טמא, starting with the first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says there are 'two' kinds that are really 'four', and then starts listing them. In the first case the person forgot only that he was טמא, but he still remembered the food was holy. The משנה goes on with more cases after this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness of טומאה, meaning the person knowing he is טמא
And it was hidden from him, meaning he forgot
The holy thing, meaning holy food from the קרבנות

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not mean someone who stayed fully aware. It means someone who knew at first and then forgot, so his sin happened by accident.

phrases.english: משנה: Awareness of טומאה
is two that are four:
He became טמא and he knew it,
and then the טומאה was hidden from him,
but he remembered that it was holy;

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ יְדִיעוֹת הַטּוּמְאָה שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Awareness of טומאה has two kinds that are really four. The first case is someone who knew he was טמא, forgot it, but remembered the food was holy.

steps.title: More cases of forgetting with holy food
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds two more cases for holy food: he forgot that the food was קודש, or he forgot both. In all these cases he brings a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he forgot the food was holy but remembered he was טמא, or he forgot both, and he ate the holy food without knowing, and found out after eating, he brings a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the list it began in step 14. It adds the other ways a person can forget while eating קודש, then gives the ruling for all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 he forgot his טומאה. Now he forgets that the food was קודש, or he forgets both facts. Either way he ate without realizing and only learned the truth afterward, so he brings a קרבן עולה ויורד to atone.

keyTerms.meaning: It was hidden from him, meaning he forgot it
Holy food, such as meat from a קרבן
This and that, meaning both facts
A 'rising and falling' offering, whose price depends on how much money the person has

steps.confusionAlert: Every one of these cases starts with the person KNOWING he was טמא. The forgetting happens later. Knowing at the start and finding out at the end are both needed for the קרבן.

phrases.english: If the holy food was hidden from him
but he remembers the impurity;
or if both this and that were hidden from him;
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means both his טומאה and the fact that the food was holy.

phrases.english: and he ate the holy food and did not know,
and after he ate, he knew,
he brings a sliding-scale offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶעְלַם מִמֶּנּוּ הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְזָכוּר אֶת הַטּוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the holy-food cases that step 14 began, and gives the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a person ate קודש while he had forgotten his טומאה, or the food's holiness, or both, and found out afterward, he brings a קרבן עולה ויורד.

steps.title: The same cases for entering the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה repeats the pattern for entering the מקדש. He forgot his טומאה, or forgot he was in the מקדש, or forgot both. If he found out after leaving, he brings a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he became טמא and knew it, then forgot his טומאה but remembered the מקדש, or forgot the מקדש but remembered the טומאה, or forgot both, and he entered the מקדש without knowing, and found out after he left, he brings a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now applies the same kinds of forgetting to a different sin: entering the מקדש while טמא. The ruling is the same as for eating קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the second 'two' of the 'two that are four' from step 14. Food and the מקדש are the two areas, and each has two kinds of forgetting: the טומאה or the holy thing. Forgetting both is grouped with them and has the same law.

phrases.english: If he became impure and knew it,
and then the impurity was hidden from him
but he remembers the Temple;
or if the Temple was hidden from him
but he remembers the impurity;
or if both this and that were hidden from him;
and he entered the Temple and did not know,
and after he left, he knew,
he brings a sliding-scale offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִטְמָא וְיָדַע, וְנֶעֶלְמָה מִמֶּנּוּ טוּמְאָה וְזָכוּר אֶת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same forgetting cases from the food section to entering the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a person entered the מקדש while he had forgotten his טומאה, or the מקדש, or both, and found out after leaving, he brings a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'four' kinds of forgetting are: food, forgot the טומאה; food, forgot the קודש; מקדש, forgot the טומאה; מקדש, forgot the מקדש. Forgetting both counts the same way.

steps.title: The added part of the עזרה counts as fully holy
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that entering the added part of the עזרה is the same as entering the original עזרה. The reason is that additions are only made through a special group: a king, a נביא, the אורים ותומים, a סנהדרין of 71, two תודה offerings, and song.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the same whether one enters the עזרה or enters the addition to the עזרה, because additions to ירושלים or the עזרות are made only with a king, a נביא, the אורים ותומים, a סנהדרין of seventy-one, two תודות, and song.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines which area counts as the מקדש for this law. It says the added part of the עזרה is just as holy as the original part, and it explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think an add-on area is less holy than the original עזרה. The משנה says no: additions can only be made through a very serious official process. Because of that, the new area gets the full holiness of the עזרה, and entering it while טמא carries the same penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: An addition that was later added onto the courtyard
The sacred device in the כהן גדול's breastplate, used to ask questions of ה׳

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the holy areas of ירושלים and the מקדש can grow while keeping full holiness: only through the proper national authorities and ceremony.

phrases.english: It is the same whether one enters the courtyard
or one enters the addition to the courtyard,
because additions are not made to the city
or to the courtyards
except with a king and a prophet
and the Urim VeTummim
and a Sanhedrin of seventy-one,
and with two thanks-offerings and with song.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד הַנִּכְנָס לָעֲזָרָה וְאֶחָד הַנִּכְנָס לְתוֹסֶפֶת הָעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines which area counts as the מקדש for the entry law in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The added part of the עזרה has the full holiness of the עזרה, because additions are made only through a king, a נביא, the אורים ותומים, a סנהדרין of 71, two תודות, and song.

steps.title: The order of the procession
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the ceremony for adding holy area: the בית דין walks in front, the two תודה offerings follow them, and all of כלל ישראל follows behind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the בית דין walks, and the two תודות come after them, and all of ישראל follows behind them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a short description of the order of the procession used to make the area holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds detail to the 'two תודות' and 'song' mentioned in step 17. It shows that the process is a public, organized ceremony that involves the leaders and the whole nation.

phrases.english: And the court walks,
and the two thanks-offerings come after them,
and all of Israel follows behind them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the details of the ceremony mentioned in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the ceremony, the בית דין walks first, the two תודות follow, and all of ישראל walks behind them.
